name: wikipedia-signs
attribution: Adapted from Wikipedia, "Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Signs_of_AI_writing), by Wikipedia contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0. Rule wording is a derivative work and is redistributed under CC BY-SA 4.0.

rules.message: 'delve' is the single most over-represented verb in model prose; prefer 'look at', 'examine', 'dig into'.

matching: let us delve into the data

rules.attribution: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing § Language and grammar (CC BY-SA 4.0)

rules.pattern: \b(tapestr(y|ies)|testament|realms?|myriad|plethora|paradigms?|interplay|treasure trove|indelible mark|focal point|valuable insights?|key turning point|profound impact)\b
rules.message: Noun that spikes far above human base rates in model prose. Name the thing plainly.
rules.attribution: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing § Language and grammar (CC BY-SA 4.0)

rules.message: Inflated verb typical of model prose; a plain verb ('shows', 'gathers', 'supports') carries the same meaning.
rules.attribution: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing § Language and grammar (CC BY-SA 4.0)

rules.message: Evaluative adjective that asserts importance instead of showing it.
rules.attribution: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing § Content (CC BY-SA 4.0)

rules.message: Model-favoured word that also has a legitimate technical sense; weighted down in the technical register. 'robust' and 'comprehensive' were removed in 0.3.0: they fired on human formal prose as often as machine prose.
rules.attribution: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing § Language and grammar (CC BY-SA 4.0)

rules.pattern: \b(nestled|in the heart of|natural beauty|diverse array|rich (heritage|history|cultural|tradition)|steeped in|must[- ]visit|boasts an?\b|world[- ]class|best[- ]in[- ]class|industry[- ]leading|enterprise[- ]grade|next[- ]generation|commitment to (excellence|quality|innovation|sustainability))
rules.message: Promotional register: the sentence advertises rather than informs.
rules.attribution: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing § Content (CC BY-SA 4.0)

rules.message: Copula avoidance: an inflated verb where 'is' would do.

matching: the plan serves as a map

rules.attribution: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing § Language and grammar (CC BY-SA 4.0)

rules.message: Trailing participle clause that editorialises about the fact it follows. Cut the clause or make the claim a sentence.

matching: sales doubled, reflecting the broader trend
it shipped in May, marking a key turning point
they hired six people, underscoring the demand
clean: it shipped in May, and the team took a week off

rules.attribution: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing § Content (CC BY-SA 4.0)

rules.message: Negative parallelism ('not just X, but Y'). State the positive claim once.

matching: it is not just a tool, it is a partner
not only structured but also flexible

rules.attribution: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing § Language and grammar (CC BY-SA 4.0)

rules.pattern: ^[ \t]*(in conclusion|in summary|to sum up|in essence|overall|ultimately|all in all)\b[,: ]
rules.message: Essay-scaffold summary opener. Delete it and let the paragraph stand.

clean: We concluded the review in March.

rules.attribution: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing § Content (CC BY-SA 4.0)

rules.pattern: \bdespite (its|these|the) (challenges|obstacles|setbacks|criticisms?|limitations|shortcomings)\b|\bfac(e|es|ed|ing) (several|a number of|numerous|significant) challenges\b|^#{1,6} +(challenges and|future outlook|awards and recognition)\b
rules.message: Outline-shaped 'challenges / future outlook' closing move, a stock model ending.

matching: Despite these challenges, the project continues to grow

rules.attribution: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing § Content (CC BY-SA 4.0)

rules.message: Emoji used as heading decoration — a formatting habit of chat interfaces, not of documents.

clean: the rocket emoji is documented below

rules.attribution: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing § Style (CC BY-SA 4.0)

rules.message: Bold-term-colon bullet list — the model's default way to fake structure.
rules.attribution: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing § Style (CC BY-SA 4.0)

rules.message: Curly double quote. Plain-text sources use straight quotes; curly ones arrive by copy-paste from a chat surface.
rules.attribution: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing § Style (CC BY-SA 4.0)

rules.pattern: \ba (crucial|pivotal|vital|significant|key|central) (role|moment|part)\b|\bplay(s|ed|ing)? an? (crucial|pivotal|vital|significant|key|important) role\b|\breflect(s|ed|ing)? (a )?broader\b|\bsymboliz(e|es|ing)? its (ongoing|enduring|lasting)\b|\bcontributing to the\b|\b(marking|shaping) the\b|\bdeeply rooted\b|\bsetting the stage for\b|\bleft an? (indelible|lasting) (mark|impression)\b
rules.message: Puffed-up significance claim: asserts that the subject matters to a broader story without adding a fact.

matching: the port played a crucial role in the region
reflecting broader trends in the industry
contributing to the growth of the sector
a tradition deeply rooted in the valley
clean: the port handled 4.2 million tonnes in 2025
the roots reach two metres down

rules.attribution: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing § Undue emphasis on significance, legacy, and broader trends (CC BY-SA 4.0)

rules.message: Over-represented model vocabulary. A plain word carries the same meaning.

matching: its enduring legacy in the field
a profound impact on the sector

rules.attribution: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing § High density of "AI vocabulary" words (CC BY-SA 4.0)

rules.message: Vague attribution: an opinion assigned to unnamed people. Name the source or drop the claim.

matching: Observers have cited the delay as a warning
Some critics argue the design is unsafe
It is widely regarded as the standard
clean: Bert Boerland argues the question is wrong.
Two of the five reviewers objected.

rules.attribution: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing § Vague attributions and overgeneralization of opinions (CC BY-SA 4.0)

rules.message: Vague expression of connection. Name the relation: caused, funded, replaced, reported to.

matching: arrested in connection with the theft
clean: he reports to the platform lead

rules.attribution: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing § Vague expression of connection or association (CC BY-SA 4.0)

rules.pattern: \bup to my last (training )?(update|refresh)\b|\bwhile specific details are (limited|scarce|sparse|unavailable)\b|\bnot widely (available|documented|disclosed|reported)\b|\bin the (provided|available|given) (sources|search results|documents|context)\b|\bbased on (the )?available information\b|\bas of my (knowledge|training)\b
rules.message: Knowledge-cutoff hedge: the model reporting on its own sources. Delete it, or state what you actually checked.

matching: While specific details are limited, the project appears active
not widely documented in the provided sources
clean: The registry lists no release after 2024.
We could not find a changelog.

rules.attribution: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing § Knowledge-cutoff disclaimers and speculation about gaps in sources (CC BY-SA 4.0)

rules.pattern: ^[ \t]*(Of course|Certainly|Absolutely|Sure thing)[!.]|\bwould you like (me to|a|an|the)\b|\bmore detailed breakdown\b|\blet me know\b|\bI cannot (offer|provide|give) (medical|legal|financial|professional) advice\b|\bI'?m sorry,? but I\b|\bI can'?t help with that, but I can\b
rules.message: Chat-turn residue: an answer to a prompt, left in a document. Delete it.

matching: Of course! The three options are listed below.
Would you like me to expand this section?
I'm sorry, but I cannot verify that
clean: Of course the build fails without the token.
Ask the team to expand it.

rules.attribution: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing § Collaborative communication (CC BY-SA 4.0)

rules.message: Word the Wikipedia guide lists as over-used by models, but common in honest writing too. Check whether it earns its place. Narrowed in 0.4.0: 'significant', 'highlight', 'enhance', 'rich' and 'key <noun>' were dropped - they read as ordinary human marketing and mail as often as machine prose.
rules.attribution: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing § High density of "AI vocabulary" words (CC BY-SA 4.0)

rules.message: Heading in Title Case where the document otherwise uses sentence case.
rules.attribution: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing § Style (CC BY-SA 4.0)
